scope: Read-only inspection; no tests, originals, credentials, network or model calls
root_cause: Identity discovery normalizes HK query aliases and returns the verified snapshot security_id 09896.
CWP query_local shares SourceResolver._identity_matches, which strips leading zeroes without market qualification, and correctly accepts the observed HK 9896 for this request.
CWP describe_candidate emits the observed manifest security_id 9896 unchanged.
FF validate_source_candidate rechecks market/security_id by raw string equality against the identified company identity 09896, rejecting a source already matched by its identity owner.
This is a cross-layer identity representation contract inconsistency, not an absent original, failed byte verification, wrong period, publication/as-of issue, or model failure.

recommended_boundary.owner: CWP source identity domain owns strict market/security representation and equivalence; FF consumes its canonical public candidate identity and keeps structural/ref/period checks.
recommended_boundary.public_projection: Make SourceCandidate market/security_id a canonical matching projection using the same pure market-aware identity helper used by resolver matching. Keep describe_version/raw source facts unchanged and diagnostic. Do not mutate an observed manifest to agree with a request.
recommended_boundary.alternative_if_contract_requires_literal: Add one explicit canonical identity projection to the CWP public candidate contract and consume that in FF; do not independently strip zeroes in FF. This is larger wire-contract work and requires compatibility fixtures.
recommended_boundary.strictness: HK numeric exchange codes up to five digits may pad to five. CN exchange codes need their existing market-specific width rules. US or unrecognized identity namespaces must not silently lose meaningful leading zeroes/class punctuation. Discovery aliases remain broader than strict source-security equivalence.
recommended_boundary.unknowns: Do not infer market, issuer or missing security from folder names. Conflicted known identities remain conflicts; missing auxiliary metadata follows existing anchored-issuer behavior, without a new permission gate.
